slots.__baseline_prompt__: Create a staged photographic fashion portrait of fictional military satire: solemn military discipline becomes absurd over an ordinary object. A performer visually guided by the supplied portrait conducts an exaggerated ceremonial inspection. Carry the reference's visible facial features and short dark bob into the main performer. She is a fictional adult woman wearing a scarlet beret, a sharply fitted olive parade jacket with comically oversized gold shoulder braid and rows of plain brass medallions, red athletic shorts and white cotton gloves. Her polished composure and softly parted lips give the image a subtle personal attraction, subordinate to the deadpan absurdity. In a spare barracks changing room with a row of empty metal lockers, she presents one ordinary black combat boot on a small square velvet-topped trophy plinth held at chest level. Her left palm supports the flat underside of the plinth, fingers curled visibly around its lower edge; the boot sole rests flat on the velvet top. The boot toe points toward her right. Her right elbow stays near her ribs, and her raised right index fingertip visibly touches the upper leather of the boot toe in a meticulous white-glove inspection. Her other right fingers curl loosely above the boot, spatially separate from its surface. Her lowered eyes scrutinize that exact contact with grave ceremonial concentration, as though a scuff might invalidate a grand decoration. The serious face, inflated regalia and humble inspected boot form the visual joke. Photograph from slightly to the performer's right at chest height, with a three-quarter view that shows the right fingertip-to-leather contact and the supporting left palm together. Vertical mid-thigh portrait, face large enough for reference comparison, hands and the entire plinth within the frame. A broad soft side light shapes her face and tailored waist, while a narrow reflection describes the boot leather; muted locker gray and olive let scarlet and brass punctuate the frame. Fine skin texture, cotton weave, polished leather and believable cloth weight, with editorial precision and a deliberately staged theatrical stillness.

slots.__baseline_prompt__: An observational photograph of fictional Korean marines enacting military black comedy: a pompous ceremonial response to a trivial mishap. A faded olive minibus has stopped on a sunlit coastal road, its near rear tire visibly squashed against the asphalt; a small unattached spare wheel stands upright a few steps in front of it, waiting to be fitted. The central woman uses the supplied portrait as a face-and-hair appearance guide, retaining its soft oval face, dark eyes, short dark cheek-length bob and lightly separated fringe. In a plain red marine training shirt, loose camouflage trousers and dusty boots, she stands to the left of the spare wheel and grips one wooden ceremonial flagpole with both hands, her forearms visibly joining the grip. Its broad red fabric hangs from a crossbar and projects a distinct patch of shade across the spare wheel. Her nearly level face turns toward the other marine with a tiny suppressed smile, the sunlight catching the unforced warmth of her eyes. To the right, a separate stocky marine stands rigidly at attention and gives the spare wheel a solemn hand salute; his face and torso turn down toward that wheel as if this ordinary repair deserved a parade. The wheel, the flag shade, both connected grips and the saluting figure read together across the foreground. The minibus, the road continuing toward the sea, and a small open toolbox establish an interrupted journey. A medium-wide, eye-level view keeps her face legible and the vehicle failure visible, with bright dry daylight, tactile roadside dust and a deadpan road-movie stillness.
